text: In a conventional (vertically illuminated) photodiode, making the absorber layer thicker improves both the transit-time bandwidth and the quantum efficiency at the same time.
explanation: False: a thicker absorber raises quantum efficiency (more photons absorbed) but lengthens carrier transit time, lowering the transit-time-limited bandwidth — a direct tradeoff. The waveguide photodetector geometry is what decouples these, absorbing along the propagation axis while keeping the depletion region thin.
